* fix: put a listed folder's unprojected file rows on the focus file leg

A ChildRef mirrors no size or mtime, so a folder listing paints those rows
off nothing until each child's own record resolves. Only the desktop drove
that leg, from a lookup on a file with no size; a host that stats no row of
its own -- the web -- left every row a device never downloaded blank.

Opening a folder now queues its direct file children that the base projects
no size for, in child order, through note_focus_file. The MAX_FOCUS_FILES
bound and the staleness damping are unchanged, so a large listing costs one
window of resolves rather than one per row, and a re-open inside the
threshold costs nothing. Both open paths run it: the FUSE-op TTL check and
the SetFocus command, the latter after its folder leg so a child that pass
has just listed joins the queue too.

Closes #855.

fix: run the focus file leg on navigation so a listed folder paints its sizes at once (#1785)

* fix: run the focus file leg on navigation so a listed folder paints its sizes at once

A folder opened from a device that never downloaded its files showed a
placeholder size and modified time for up to one poll cadence plus one resolve
per row. The navigation path ran the folder leg and queued the size-less file
children, but only the tick loop drained that queue.

The on-access refresh now runs the file leg itself, after the folder leg and
after the queueing step, so a row the folder leg has just listed joins the same
pass. It runs under the vault's own scope root only, keeps the existing
MAX_FOCUS_FILES bound and staleness damping, and takes a file off the queue only
when the pass attempted it, as the tick loop does.

* refactor: announce each on-access read leg's own base change

One announcement after both legs held the folder listing behind the file leg it
had just fed. Each leg now settles through one helper that stamps, holds the
unlinks it observed, and announces a base that moved, as the tick's legs do.

* refactor: settle every focus read leg through one function

The tick loop and the navigation path each held their own copy of the settle
rule: hold what the leg saw depart, stamp what it attempted, announce a base it
moved. Both now call one free function that returns the verdict the tick still
folds.

The navigation leg also reads the vault root once and filters both legs against
that one reading, so the scope its seed opens and the scope it admits nodes from
cannot come from either side of the seed lookup.

* test: pin the repeat-navigation damper on a row that projects no size

The row the test used had published a version, so the first navigation gave it a
size and the size filter in the queueing step was what kept the repeat visit off
the record plane. The staleness stamp was never reached. The row is now one that
published no version, so it projects no size however often a pass resolves it
and only the stamp can hold the second visit back. Removing the damper fails the
test.

* fix: queue the file children the tick's folder leg lists so a remote add paints its size

The tick fixed its file targets before its folder leg ran, so a file
another device added to a folder held in focus was listed but never
resolved. The pass now queues the size-less file children of the folders
in view after the folder leg settles, then takes that scope's file
targets from the queue and runs the file leg in the same pass.

Folds the simplify pass: one scope-filter helper for the tick legs and the
navigation path, the file targets read straight from the focus queue instead
of a second cross-scope grouping, and a scope whose only folder in view is its
own root now gets a pass of its own.

The queueing step refills the focus queue on every scope leg, so a pass could
spend MAX_FOCUS_FILES resolves per leg. The blueprint bounds the burst per
tick. Each leg now takes only what earlier legs left of that budget, and never
a row the pass already attempted.

<result>I found no web e2e spec that checks a file row's SIZE or MODIFIED cell, in the smoke slice or the full suite. The page object already has a helper to read those cells, but no spec in `tests/web-e2e` calls it. The only test that reads them is a cross-client scenario that runs on the main gate only, and even that reads them in a tab that joined the vault while it was still empty.

## 1. Suite location, slices, gates

- **Where it lives:** `tests/web-e2e/`. Local specs are in `tests/`, staging specs in `staging/`, the soak in `staging/soak/`.
- **How the slices split** (`tests/web-e2e/playwright.config.ts`):
  - `E2E_SUITE` defaults to `smoke` (:20). Smoke drops every test tagged `@full`: `grepInvert: /@full/` (:129). `full` runs everything.
  - The `e2e` project picks up every spec except `release-bundle.spec.ts` (:111-116), so a new untagged test joins smoke automatically.
  - Per-test timeout is 120s (:108), with `retries: 0` (:130).
- **Who runs each slice:**
  - **Smoke:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:459-470` (`Web E2E Smoke`, `suite: smoke`), reported through `Web E2E Smoke Result` (:472-491). It blocks every PR merge (`blueprint/testing.md:258`).
  - **Full:** `.github/workflows/ci-e2e.yml:100-108` on push to main (a revert-first gate, `testing.md:259`) and `tag-staging.yml:49-58`.
  - Both call the reusable `.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml`. The test step timeout there is **12 min for smoke and 30 for full** (:191-195).
- **Tests in the smoke slice** (everything not tagged `@full`; the README lists them at `tests/web-e2e/README.md:59-63`):
  - `smoke.spec.ts`: all 6 tests
  - `write-path.spec.ts`: all 5 tests
  - `device-approval.spec.ts`: all 5
  - `cross-client.spec.ts`, `contact-grant.spec.ts`, `write-grant.spec.ts`, `shared.spec.ts`: 1 each
  - `sharing.spec.ts:15` (the first test only)
  - `settings.spec.ts:77,102`
  - `link-first.spec.ts:171` (steps 1-3)
  - `release-bundle.spec.ts` (3 tests, `release` project)
  - Everything in `bin`, `save-path` and `invite`, plus the rest of `sharing`, `settings` and `link-first`, is `@full`.

## 2. Specs that assert on size or modified

- **`tests/web-e2e/tests/*` and `staging/*`: none.** A grep for `.cells(`, `file-list-item-size`, `file-list-item-date` and `'...'` finds no hits in any spec.
- **`tests/cross-client/src/scenarios/fileRoundTrip.ts:46-53, 119-143`:** polls `files.cells()` until the size reads `1.5 KB` and checks the modified label against `renderedDays`.
  - The tab joined **while the vault was empty** (:32-35: "A tab that cold-starts onto a vault the mount already published is what `second-session` covers"). So it proves the sync of a remote write, not a cold start onto an existing vault.
  - It runs only in `desktop-e2e.yml` (macOS leg) on the main gate, never in the PR gate.
- **`tests/cross-client/src/scenarios/secondSession.ts:67-70`:** does cold-start a fresh tab onto a populated vault, but only checks names (`listsInFolder`). It never reads size or modified.
- **`apps/web/src/vault/useFolderNavigation.test.tsx:115-143`:** a unit test with a fake engine. It shows that `...` flips to `2 KB` when the snapshot carries a size. It says nothing about whether the real engine delivers the size.
- **Same-session uploads** (`write-path.spec.ts:62-80`, `link-first.spec.ts:104`, `save-path`, `contact-grant`, `write-grant`): these only check that the row is visible and read back the bytes. They never read the cells. Any size they would see could come from the local op echo or `UploadListItem`.

## 3. Helpers

- **`tests/web-e2e/vault.ts`**
  - `coldStart(page, signIn?)` (:50): opens the page, waits for service-worker control, signs in, waits for `settled`.
  - `drained(files, vault)` (:71)
  - `refreshedUntil(vault, locator, count, timeout)` (:85)
  - `nodeOf`, `namesOf`, `PAYLOAD`
- **`tests/web-e2e/devices.ts`**
  - `freshLogin()` (:27): mints the login secret and account id in the test process.
  - `Device.open(browser, login)` (:54): a **new `BrowserContext`**, so fresh IndexedDB, locks and service worker.
  - `device.online()` (:77): cold start as the same account.
  - `device.offline()` (:88), `device.close()` (:92)
  - `link-first.spec.ts:39-49` already wraps these in a `device` fixture that closes every context it opened.
- **`tests/web-e2e/page-objects/vault.page.ts`**
  - `open`, `ready`, `controlled`
  - `coldStart()` (:44): a random account in the same context.
  - `joinAs(accountId)` (:59), `signInHere` (:69)
  - `refresh()` (:78): the no-cache pass.
  - `settled()` (:112), `read(name)` (:131), `events()`
- **`tests/web-e2e/page-objects/files.page.ts`**
  - `upload(name, bytes)` (:196)
  - `row(name)` (:90), `names()` (:97)
  - `published()` (:56): waits until no row carries an unpublished mark.
  - **`cells(name)` (:127-134)**: returns `{size, modified}` read from `.file-list-item-size` and `.file-list-item-date`. Its doc comment already says an unresolved row paints `...`.
  - `renderedDays(timestamps)` (:141)
  - `open(name)` (:117), `toRoot()` (:106)
- **Clearing site data:** there is no dedicated helper. A fresh context via `Device.open` or `browser.newContext()` does the job (as in `invite.spec.ts:52,98`).

## 4. How `apps/web` renders the cells

- **Component:** `apps/web/src/components/file-browser/FileListItem.tsx:59-66`.
  - `<span className="file-list-item-size" role="gridcell">{row.size}</span>`
  - `<span className="file-list-item-date" role="gridcell">{row.modified}</span>`
  - Neither cell has a `data-testid`. The row itself is `data-testid="file-list-item"` with `role="row"` and `data-node-id` (:24-27).
- **Placeholder:** `apps/web/src/vault/listing.ts:13` defines `const UNRESOLVED = '...'`.
  - `projectedSize` / `projectedDate` return it when `child.size` or `child.mtime` is `null` (:84-90).
  - Folders show `-` for size (:16, :72).
- **Other rows with these classes:** `ParentDirRow.tsx:31-34`, and `UploadListItem.tsx:84` (the in-flight upload row, which shows `formatBytes(upload.size)` from local data).

## 5. Proposed spec (smoke)

Add one untagged test to `tests/web-e2e/tests/write-path.spec.ts`, reusing link-first's `device` fixture.

1. Create `login = freshLogin()` and open device A. Run `online()`, then `files.upload('cold.bin', 2048 bytes)` and `files.published()`, then `offline()` and `close()`.
2. Open device B with `Device.open(browser, login)`, a new context with empty stores. Run `online()`.
3. Assert the row `cold.bin` is visible.
4. Poll `files.cells('cold.bin')` with no manual `refresh`, so the cold-start sync alone has to fill the cells. Expect `size` to be `'2 KB'` (as in the unit test) and `modified` to be neither `'...'` nor `'-'`, within about 60s.

- **Capture discipline**: redirect the run to a log and append `EXIT_CODE=$?`; never pipe through `tail`/`tee` (masks exit codes). Playwright wipes `test-results/` per run — harvest failure screenshots BEFORE any re-run. This config writes no usable `.last-run.json` for full runs — don't build watchdogs on it.

# Web E2E

The PR gate's smoke slice: `apps/web` driven in a real browser against a real
API, a real engine, and the hermetic `/routing/v1` record store. Wired as the
merge-blocking `Web E2E Smoke` job (`.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml`), reported
through the stable `Web E2E Smoke Result` context in `ci.yml`.

Normative source: [`blueprint/testing.md`](../../blueprint/testing.md).

## What it covers

- the front door renders every built login method
- an unauthenticated deep link is returned to the front door and lists no vault
  contents
- a cold start reaches a settled, empty vault at its root; the chrome renders
  it, and the event taps saw the snapshot that produced it
- folder create, rename, move and delete, each ending on a drained queue that
  carries no dead letter — so a write that never published fails the gate
- an upload and the file read back off the network, asserted byte for byte
- signing out returns the tab to the front door
- the settings route opens from the sidebar and names the signed-in account
- a session end — a sign-out or a forget-this-device — reaches every tab of the
  origin, and no promoted sibling re-exports a secret to cold-start a
  replacement engine with
- a folder's share dialog reads the engine's grant list, and the invite link it
  mints names the claim route, is shown once, and leaves a scope behind that
  the engine then refuses a second link on
- the contact import refuses what it cannot read, and leaving the step retires
  the refusal
- an invite link minted by one vault is claimed by a second account in its own
  browser context, and the minter converts that claim into a read grant
- a write grant made by a hand exchange of contact codes lets the recipient
  upload, create a folder and delete inside the granted folder; the owner reads
  the writes back, and the delete lands in the owner's bin
- a saved settings record reads back off the vault field by field, with the
  provider credential offered for clearing rather than shown
- two sessions carry a device approval end to end: both devices derive the same
  comparison value, an approval hands the requester the exact factor the
  approver minted, a denial and an abandon each end the rendezvous, and a
  substituted ephemeral key shows other digits and seals a factor the honest
  device cannot open
- the shipping bundle exposes no introspection hook
- the link-first flow across two owner devices (`link-first.spec.ts`), in these
  steps:
  1. device A mints a read link with the owner name on a folder of two entries
  2. the holder previews the owner and the folder, joins, and reads both entries
     through the link's keys
  3. device B converts the claim on its tick, and the holder's row turns to a
     grant
  4. a write link holder writes after device B converts, and device A reads the
     write
  5. device A revokes the write link with its joiners: the writer fails closed
     and the reader keeps access
  6. device B cuts the reader, the reader joins again through a new link that
     device A converts, and the next re-key on device B serves it (ADR 0025 D3,
     E4)
  7. the sweep on device B cuts an expired link, and its chip leaves device A

The slices split on the `@full` tag. The smoke slice keeps login, CRUD, the
session-end pair, the device approval, one share-dialog spec, the contact, write and
cross-client grant specs, and steps 1 to 3 of the link-first flow — the
bounded-minutes budget the PR gate holds. Everything above that lands `@full`,
in the main gate's whole suite.

## How the suite logs in

There is no interactive Core Kit login in CI. The `e2e` build carries the
introspection hook (`apps/web/src/engine/introspection.ts`), which hands the
engine a login secret the test generates. Challenge-signature login creates the
account on first contact, so a fresh 32-byte secret is a fresh, isolated vault —
no fixture setup and no shared state to serialize around. A test mints a fresh
secret for every account it signs in, and a device that signs in again reuses
its account's secret (`devices.ts`).

The `release` project runs the same specs' counterpart against a bundle built
**without** the flag, and asserts `window.__CIPHERBOX_ENGINE__` is absent.

## How the suite drives two devices

`device-approval.spec.ts` gives each device its own browser context: its own
engine, and its own identity key in its own IndexedDB. One context signs in and
registers as an approver; the other stays cold, which is the state of a device
that cannot yet reconstruct.

The suite drives the shipped relay client
(`apps/web/src/auth/deviceApprovalApi.ts`) from the test process rather than from
the requester's tab, so a spec can carry something other than what the requester
cut. The rendezvous binds an account to an identity subject, so the specs mint
one real identity token through the wallet method and sign the EIP-4361 message
themselves.

Every rendezvous secret stays behind the introspection seam: a tap answers with
the public transcript and, for a factor, a SHA-256 of it.

`link-first.spec.ts` signs two devices in on one account. `devices.ts` holds the
account's login secret in the test process, and each device's context reads it
through a binding, so no `evaluate` argument and no trace carries it. A device
that must not act goes offline (its tabs close), so each conversion, cut and
sweep has exactly one owner device that can run it. A holder is a device too,
so it can sign in again on a second link.

## Running it locally

Both bundles must be built before Playwright starts; the config only serves
them.

1. Bring up Postgres, Kubo and the record store:

   ```sh
   docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d postgres ipfs mock-ipns-routing
   ```

2. Apply migrations and boot the API:

   ```sh
   export DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5432 DB_USERNAME=postgres \
     DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED DB_DATABASE=cipherbox NODE_ENV=test \
     JWT_SECRET=web-e2e-jwt-secret THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT=200 \
     KUBO_API_URL=http://localhost:5001 \

//
// `E2E_SUITE` picks the slice: `smoke` (the default) is the PR gate's
// bounded-minutes budget and drops every `@full`-tagged test; `full` is the main
// gate and runs everything; `soak` runs the staging soak (`staging/soak`)
// alone, against `E2E_BASE_URL`.

// local server, the `staging` project only, and the real login the staging
// profiles need (`staging/README` and blueprint/testing.md staging release

import { previewCommand } from './preview';

const suite = process.env.E2E_SUITE ?? 'smoke';
// Reject an unrecognized value rather than silently running the smaller slice.

  throw new Error(`E2E_SUITE must be smoke | full | soak; got "${suite}"`);
}

const E2E_PORT = 4173;
const RELEASE_PORT = 4174;

const isCi = Boolean(process.env.CI);

const url = (port: number) => `http://localhost:${port}`;

 * `reuse` is off for the release bundle even locally: reusing whatever already
 * answers on that port would make the hook-absence assertion meaningless.
 */

  command: previewCommand(outDir, port),
  url: url(port),
  reuseExistingServer: reuse && !isCi,
  timeout: 60_000,
  stdout: 'pipe' as const,
  stderr: 'pipe' as const,
});

const stagingBaseUrl = process.env.E2E_BASE_URL?.trim();

  throw new Error('E2E_SUITE=soak runs against a deployed front; set E2E_BASE_URL');
}

// No trace: a staging run holds a real session, and its report is an artifact
// of a public repository. A trace records every request header, which there
// carries the session bearer and the accelerator pseudonym — a gateway

// page can show a bearer link URL, in the share dialog or in the ledger editor.

  baseURL: stagingBaseUrl,
  trace: 'off' as const,

115:      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], baseURL: url(E2E_PORT) },
120:      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], baseURL: url(RELEASE_PORT) },
123:  webServer: [preview('dist', E2E_PORT, true), preview('dist-release', RELEASE_PORT)],
   ```

## Problem

On a cold start of the web host over a vault that already holds files, file rows keep the `...` placeholder for size and modified date. Three gaps, all in the focus file leg, the only path that resolves a file's own record and projects its size and mtime.

1. **The root was never in view.** The web names no folder for `/files` (host law: a host asks for the root, it never names one). The engine read `open_folder: None` as no folder in view, so the root's file rows were never queued, on the tick or on navigation. `FocusWindow::folders_in_view_or_root` puts the current root in navigation's slot when no folder is open; the tick's `refresh_focus` and `refresh_focus_on_access` use it. The root is read at use time, so a root cut needs no host action.
2. **The navigation file leg skipped a shared folder's rows.** `refresh_focus_on_access` ran one leg under the vault root's scope and dropped every queued row whose scope root is a descendant scope, leaving them for the next 30 s poll tick. `navigation_file_legs` now runs one leg per scope the queued rows belong to, under that scope's own seed and floors, with a grafted plane when the scope is not the vault's own, as the tick does. A scope with no seed held keeps its rows queued.
3. **A focus before the first pass accused an honest writer.** `start` returns before any pass, and only the pass's boundary walk installs the descendant scopes. A `SetFocus` on a shared folder that arrived first read it under the root seed, and the adoption gate reported a false attributable abuse. `TickPass::walk_boundaries` runs the root adopt and the scope walk once, inline, before such a navigation's folder leg; `SessionState::boundary_walk_ran` makes it a once-per-session cost.

None of these findings is a vulnerability that an attacker can exploit. No row is ever adopted under the wrong seed, so data stays fail-closed. Finding 1 is a defect in trust reporting: it can send a false abuse report against an honest writer.

## Finding 1, MEDIUM: the item 3 fix is narrowed, not complete

**Where:** `crates/engine/src/sync/pass.rs:483`, `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:8686`

**Mechanism:** `walk_scopes` sets `boundary_walk_ran` to true before it does its work. `descendant_scope_roots` is filled only after the walk's awaits finish, and only when the walk returns `Ok`. Three paths leave the flag true while the set stays empty:

- **(a) A pass is mid-walk.** The tick loop is a spawned task and does not take the command write lock (`crates/wasm/src/host.rs`). A `SetFocus` that arrives while the first pass awaits inside `descendant_scope_roots` sees the flag as true and skips the inline walk.
- **(b) The walk fails.** The walk returns `Err`, which includes `WalkFailure::Unavailable` on a cold network.
- **(c) The walk never starts.** `held_root` or `sweep_keys` is `None`, and `walk_scopes` returns at once.

**Failure:** In each case `navigation_file_legs` gives a shared folder's rows to the root scope. It reads them under the vault seed, the child gate rejects them, and the engine emits a false attributable-abuse event. This is the bug that item 3 sets out to fix.

**Fix:**
1. Set the flag only after `install_descendant_scopes`, on `Ok`. Rename it to state that meaning, for example `boundary_walk_landed`.
2. In `refresh_focus_on_access`, do not run the inline walk again while that flag is false. Skip the folder and file legs and keep the rows queued for the tick. A retry on each `SetFocus` would run a full root adopt and walk on every navigation, with no `stale_after` damping.

## Finding 2, LOW: the inline walk can overlap a pass's root adopt

**Where:** `crates/engine/src/sync/pass.rs:222-229`

**Mechanism:** If a pass that a cadence or an earlier command started has not yet reached `walk_scopes`, the inline walk runs `refresh_floors`, `adopt_root` and `walk_scopes` at the same time as that pass.

**Failure:**
- The inline adopt is `CacheFirst`. If it reads sequence N after the pass has committed floor N+1, `resolve.rs` reports a strictly older sequence as a `TrustViolation`. That is a false trust event on the vault root.
- `deposit_seed` overwrites without a check. The `Current` arm can therefore write back an older read seed that has a lower stamp. This heals itself: the next `refresh_seed_floor` evicts it.

**Fix:** Skip the inline walk while a pass is in flight. `sync_status.reconcile_started` is a candidate in-flight marker. The fix for finding 1 removes most of this window.

## Finding 3, LOW (freshness, not security): on desktop, root rows push out the rows of folders in use

**Where:** `crates/engine/src/sync/tick.rs:128`, `crates/engine/src/sync/pass.rs:688`

- Desktop never sets `open_folder`, so the root now always takes navigation's slot.

It is what an owner re-key consults to tell a descendant the owner cut from one it granted independently; an ancestor's cut never carries down on its own. The cut epoch is the scope-wide complement: it refuses the whole pre-cut set at the gate, while this floor withholds one recipient's blob at a re-key. Device-local, and it only rises except by the clear below; unlike the epoch and sequence floors it has **no cold-seed anchor**: no owner-signed record carries it, so a device that holds no floor yet takes the first commitment it is served. An owner-signed commitment that commits the recipient again, at a cut epoch not below the one this device recorded for its cut, clears this device's floor for that recipient (ADR 0025 D3). The clear removes this device's recorded cut for the recipient; the grant floor does not change, because a re-key withholds a blob only when a recorded cut is newer than the grant floor. A device that did not make the cut raises the cut epoch from the first post-cut record it resolves, whether or not it can adopt that record.
57:- **Bin-held key** — the key a soft delete re-keys the doomed subtree under, from the `bin-held-key` edge. It sits outside every scope's derivation, which is the access cut key regression cannot give. Scope-seed shaped: every node of the subtree keys at `readKey(nodeSeed(held, nodeId))`, so the one key the entry carries opens the whole subtree.
71:- **Deadline** — the owner-signed time on a link entry by which an owner device must convert a claim. Conversion checks it once, at the ack, and stores the verdict. A link holder's read checks it at the join and on every refresh pass. The claimant stops its re-posts at it. An owner sweep cuts a link whose deadline has passed (ADR 0023 D3, D6, ADR 0024 D5, ADR 0025 D2).
